items.sentence: Jom ___ in Quezon City since 2020.
items.why: 'Since 2020' points to a time that continues until now, so use present perfect 'has lived'.

items.sentence: Lyka ___ the jeepney to school two hours ago.
items.why: 'Ago' names a finished past time, so use simple past 'took'.

items.sentence: We ___ already finished our group project for science.
items.why: 'Already' with a result that matters now takes present perfect 'have finished'.

items.sentence: Marco ___ eaten his merienda yet, so he is hungry.
items.why: 'Yet' goes with present perfect, so use 'hasn't eaten'.

items.sentence: By the time Kuya Ron arrived, the game ___ already started.
items.why: The game started before another past action, so use past perfect 'had started'.

items.sentence: Bea ___ load before the typhoon knocked out the signal.
items.why: Buying happened before another past event, so past perfect 'had bought' is right.

items.sentence: Look at those dark clouds; it ___ going to rain.
items.why: When you see signs now of what will happen, use 'is going to'.

items.sentence: Don't worry, I ___ help you carry the sacks of rice.
items.why: An offer decided on the spot uses 'will'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena ___ as a caregiver in Dubai for three years now.
items.why: 'For three years now' means it started in the past and still continues, so use 'has worked'.

items.sentence: Last fiesta, the barangay ___ a big basketball tournament.
items.why: 'Last fiesta' is a finished time, so use simple past 'held'.

items.sentence: The box of mangoes ___ too heavy for Jom to carry.
items.why: The subject is 'box', not 'mangoes', so the verb is 'is'.

items.sentence: The players on our team ___ practicing for the intramurals.
items.why: The subject is 'players', which is plural, so use 'are'.

items.sentence: One of the jeepney drivers ___ Lyka's uncle.
items.why: 'One' is the real subject and it is singular, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Our class ___ going to the museum on Friday.
items.why: 'Class' is one group acting together, so it takes the singular 'is'.

items.sentence: Fifty pesos ___ enough for merienda at the canteen.
items.why: An amount of money counts as one sum, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Noli Me Tangere ___ required reading for Grade 9 students.
items.why: A title is one thing, so it takes the singular 'is'.

items.sentence: The family ___ dinner together every Sunday after mass.
items.why: 'Family' is one group acting together, so use the singular 'eats'.

items.sentence: The list of absent students ___ on the teacher's desk.
items.why: The subject is 'list', not 'students', so the verb is 'is'.

items.sentence: Each of the barangay tanods ___ a flashlight during patrol.
items.why: 'Each' is singular, so the verb is 'carries'.

items.sentence: Three hours ___ a long time to wait for a tricycle.
items.why: A length of time counts as one amount, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Jom ___ speak three languages: Tagalog, Bisaya, and English.
items.why: 'Can' shows ability, something a person is able to do.

items.sentence: His shoes are gone and the door is locked, so Marco ___ have left.
items.why: 'Must have' shows you are sure something happened because of the evidence.

items.sentence: You ___ wear your ID inside the campus; it is a school rule.
items.why: 'Have to' shows a rule or an obligation you cannot skip.

items.sentence: You look tired, so you ___ sleep early tonight.
items.why: 'Should' gives advice about the good thing to do.

items.sentence: ___ I borrow your ballpen, Ma'am?
items.why: 'May' asks for permission politely.

items.sentence: ___ you please lower the volume of your phone?
items.why: 'Could you' makes a polite request.

items.sentence: It ___ rain later, so bring an umbrella just in case.
items.why: 'Might' shows something is possible but not sure.

items.sentence: Lyka ___ already swim when she was five years old.
items.why: 'Could' is the past form of 'can' for ability.

items.sentence: Students ___ turn off their phones before the exam starts.
items.why: 'Must' shows a strong rule that has to be followed.

items.sentence: Marco failed the quiz; he ___ have studied instead of playing ML.
items.why: 'Should have' says what was the right thing to do but did not happen.

items.sentence: Each student brought ___ own baon to the field trip.
items.why: 'Each' is singular, so 'his or her' matches it.

items.sentence: Everyone in the class should bring ___ own umbrella tomorrow.
items.why: Modern English accepts 'their' for 'everyone' when we do not know the gender.

items.sentence: ___ did you text about the change in schedule?
items.why: The person is the object of 'text', so use 'whom'.

items.sentence: ___ is bringing the speaker to the fiesta tonight?
items.why: The person is doing the action, so use 'who'.

items.sentence: Neither Jom nor Marco remembered ___ password for the game.
items.why: 'Neither' makes the subject singular, so use 'his' for the two boys.

items.sentence: Lyka and I finished ___ project before the deadline.
items.why: 'Lyka and I' means 'we', so the matching pronoun is 'our'.

items.sentence: The jeepney lost ___ brakes near the public market.
items.why: 'Its' shows ownership; 'it's' means 'it is'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena, ___ works in Dubai, sends money every month.
items.why: Tita Nena is the one doing the action 'works', so use 'who'.

items.sentence: To ___ should I give the attendance sheet?
items.why: After a preposition like 'to', use 'whom'.

items.sentence: Marco and ___ are playing ML after class.
items.why: 'Marco and I' is the subject of the sentence, so use 'I'.
